why: The statement asks only for the reciprocal-sum implication for every length. Green-Tao (primes) and Bloom-Sisask (k=3) are pre-snapshot cases. Kelley-Meka, Leng-Sah-Sawhney and Raghavan bound r_k(N), a neighbouring density quantity that is not the statement's question; LSS's bound exp(-(log log N)^c_k) is not shown to reach the summability threshold, so these are variant. Green's survey is expository (none). The two OpenAI rows describe one release (the research pass and the repository stage); both claim the full statement via a dyadic summation of a density theorem, so scope whole. Nobody named has worked through the argument (Bloom explicitly did not; Gasarch only repeats the claim) and a Lean build is not digestion, so unreviewed. Doubtful rather than not_credible: there is no identified error and the reduction step is standard, but the headline density bound would be a major leap and the formal chain's content is disputed. AI role generated per the repository's own statement that the manuscripts were produced by the model; no human authors are named.
doubts: The two OpenAI events are duplicates of one release (dated 6 Oct 2026). The README attributes production to the model at collection level rather than naming family 159 individually. Bloom-Sisask's k=3 consequence for reciprocal sums rests on Quanta's description; verification left unreviewed since no named expert reading or journal acceptance is in the record.
